title: Not Me 2.0. Christ in Me.
headline: Christianity Isn’t Self-Improvement
tagline: Jesus did not die and rise merely to produce a more impressive version of the person I was determined to become.
seo_title: Christianity Isn't Self-Improvement: Galatians 2:20 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Paul didn't say Christ helped me become my best self; he said Christ lives in me. A devotional for men on Galatians 2:20 and John 3:30.
verse_text: I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me….

scriptures.text: I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me….
He must become greater; I must become less.

items: There is one final trap waiting inside almost every personal growth journey.
And eventually you build a better version of you.
But Galatians 2:20 interrupts the entire project.
Paul does not say, “Christ helped me become my best self.”
The question is no longer, “How great can I become?”
It becomes, “How fully can this life come under the lordship of Christ?”
Jesus may sharpen ambition, and remove selfish ambition.
Increase influence, and decrease your need to be noticed.
Develop leadership, and destroy your need to control.
Jesus is not committed to building the version of you your ego envisioned.

blocks.text: “Jesus exists to help me become the person I have decided I should be.”

items: Humility is not pretending you have nothing to offer. It is knowing you were never supposed to be the center.
A life can be highly optimized and badly ordered.
Even serving God can become a way of avoiding God.
The goal is not sameness. The goal is Christlikeness expressed through a surrendered life.
